question.leadin: Answer the following about the Gaza Strip.
question.text: In 1993, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed a series of accords named for this city, the capital of Norway. The accords gave Palestinians the right to self-government in Gaza.
question.clue: Works such as Monolith, which is a tower of human bodies, and Wheel of Life are contained in this city's Frogner Park, which features other stone and bronze statuary by Gustav Vigeland .

swap.leadin: Answer the following about German invasions during World War II.
swap.text: Germany invaded this country and Denmark as part of Operation Weserubung. This country was home to German heavy water production and was led by Vidkun Quisling after its surrender.
swap.clue: Another leader of this country served with Josef Terboven and was executed with Albert Hagelin after establishing a fascist government.

question.leadin: The Treaty of Nystad ended this war in 1721, 12 years after a decisive victory over Charles XII at Poltava ended Sweden's time as a European power.
question.text: Name this war motivated by one European power's desire for a port city on the Baltic Sea.
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.leadin: This member of the House of Vasa defeated Count Tilly in his most famous victory, Breitenfeld.
swap.text: Name this man who died at the Battle of Lutzen and was known as the "Lion of the North."
swap.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav Adolf; Gustav II; Gustavus the Great; prompt on “Gustav” or “Gustavus”]
swap.clue: This man allegedly claimed that "the Lord God is my armor" before fighting without protection and dying at the Battle of Lutzen.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about people whose names have become synonymous with the word traitor.
question.text: This man collaborated with the Germans after the invasion of his country, and requested to be made the 'Fuhrer of Norway'. He was found guilty of high treason by the allies and sentenced to death after the war.
question.clue: This politician launched their political career in a series of articles explaining their 'political thoughts' on the death of mentor Fritjohf Nansen.
question.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

swap.text: This prime minister of Sweden presided over the Million Programme, in which he sought to build one million public housing units. He was assassinated in Stockholm in 1986.
swap.clue: This person succeeded his mentor, the country's longest serving PM, as party leader in 1969.

question.leadin: This country once formed a dual monarchy with Norway.
question.text: Name this Scandinavian nation that was led by Christian X in the early twentieth century.
question.clue: A bishop from this kingdom ordered the destruction of pagan idols after capturing the temple of Svantovit on the Wendish-held island of Rugen; that bishop, Absalon, commissioned the history of this kingdom's people written by Saxo Grammaticus.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of paper money.
swap.text: This European country was the first to print paper money, doing so from its central bank during the reign of Carl Gustaf. That central bank was based out of this country's capital at Stockholm.
swap.clue: Gutnish is spoken on this country's largest island.

question.text: The Ghost Sonata is a play by this author of Creditors, who created the valet Jean and a demanding owner of a bird in Miss Julie.

swap.leadin: This man agreed to the Treaty of Stolbovo with Michael Romanov and was advised by Axel Oxenstierna.
swap.text: Name this Swedish ruler who won at the Battle of Breitenfeld against the forces of Johann Tilly while fighting during the Thirty Years' War.
swap.clue: This ruler ended wars with his neighbors through the treaties of Knared and Stolbovo, although he was constantly at war with his cousin, Sigismund III of Poland.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of some islands in Europe that are not Great Britain or Ireland.
question.text: This Norwegian territory's namesake treaty regulates commercial and military activities. This Arctic archipelago is home to one of the largest seed banks in the world -- the Global Seed Vault.
question.answerHtml: Svalbard [prompt on Spitsbergen; do NOT accept or prompt on “Jan Mayen”]
question.clue: The name of this Norwegian archipelago means "cold shores," and its three inhabited islands are Spitzbergen, Bear Island, and Hopen.

swap.leadin: The Archipelago Ring Road connects the cities in this country's Archipelago Sea.
swap.text: Name this Scandinavian country that contains the region of North Karelia and the Swedish-speaking Aland Islands, and which has its capital on the shore of a namesake gulf.
swap.clue: As a grand duchy, this country's capital was originally at Turku.

question.leadin: Margaret I facilitated this union by serving as regent to her great-nephew Erik of Pomerania during his minority.
question.text: Name this Scandinavian union which united three countries under a single monarch until the early 16th century.
question.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of the good old-fashioned fun of throwing sticks.
swap.text: The stick throwing game of skittles originated in a region this country shares with its eastern neighbour. A bat sport invented by a veteran of this country's Civil War was demonstrated when it hosted the 1952 Summer Olympics.
swap.clue: Activists from this country's largest Germanic minority group cited scientific racists to argue that its majority ethnicity was of inferior Mongoloid stock.

question.text: Sweden was a lot less lucky in cold weather in 1719, when Carl Gustaf Armfeldt killed over 3,000 of his troops while invading this country. Along with Denmark and Sweden, this country formed the Kalmar Union.
question.clue: The Nazi official Josef Terboven worked with a collaborationist government in this country after a German invasion forced this country's king Haakon VII to flee to Britain.

swap.text: The second False Dmitriy lost many of his supporters after the intervention of Sigismund III of the Poland-Lithuania Commonwealth, who used the confusion of the Time of Troubles as an attempt to conquer parts of Russia. Sigismund belonged to this royal house, founded after Gustav I revolted against Christian II and the Kalmar Union.
swap.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

question.leadin: Answer the following about insane CIA Cold War plots that did not involve exploding cigars or acoustic kitties.
question.text: This place was long thought to contain a lost hydrogen bomb after a secret mission crashed at Thule Air Base. Project Iceworm wanted to build launch sites under this territory of Denmark, which is the world's largest island.
question.clue: Henrik Kauffman signed a 1941 treaty with the United States paving the way for the establishment of Thule Airbase on this island.

swap.leadin: Rudiger von der Goltz described women combatants in this war by stating "Hardly have the French attacked as fiercely."
swap.text: The Jager ("YAY-ger") Battalion supported one side in what war's Battle of Antrea, which has been compared to Verdun? This conflict over a newly independent former Grand Duchy was followed by "Kinship Wars" with an eastern neighbor.
swap.answerHtml: Finnish Civil War [or Suomen sisällissota or Finska inbördeskriget; accept vapaussota; accept Citizen War or Class War or Red Rebellion; prompt on Civil War or War of Independence]
swap.clue: Veterans of this conflict launched the Aunus and Vien as part of the "Kinship Wars" in nearby countries.

question.text: In August of 1944 Mannerheim succeeded this man as president of Finland when the parliament deposed this man and appointed Mannerheim in his place.
question.clue: This prime minister of Finland who resigned and was replaced by Carl Mannerheim in 1944.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Finland during World War II.
swap.text: Paavo Tavela is one of only a handful of recipients of the highest Finnish military honor named after this man, a former president of Finland whose name is given to the line that delineates the Karelian isthmus from Russia.
swap.clue: During World War I, Finnish independence advocates often joined the German army as Jagers, a movement that this Finnish Baron opposed. This man names a fortification line built by the Finns during the Winter War.
